body:
Global crypto markets shed $2.68T in total market cap today, a figure that reflects a -3.33% drawdown in 24 hours as sentiment cooled to a Neutral 50 on the Fear & Greed index, down from 54 yesterday. Volume came in at $58.7B across the space, which is serviceable but not the kind of panic-flush number that typically marks a capitulation floor. BTC dominance held firm at 59.4%, with ETH dominance compressing further to 10.4%, a ratio that tells you rotation is not happening in favor of risk — it's simply a market leaning defensively into its largest asset while broader alts bleed. The mood is one of cautious consolidation ahead of a Fed decision rather than outright fear, but the directional bias is unambiguously lower for now.

Bitcoin printed $79,605 on the session, down -0.89% in 24 hours and -2.47% over the past 7 days, with 24-hour volume of $22.16B. The $80,000 level is the number everyone is watching, and BTC slipped below it intraday before reclaiming ground — that reclaim is real but tentative. A CoinDesk headline confirmed the slip directly, noting Bitcoin fell below $80,000 as Anthropic filed its IPO. The short-term hourly move of -0.13% suggests price is grinding rather than collapsing, which keeps the bull case alive, but a separate CoinDesk report noted a $68 million bitcoin bet targeting a post-midterm election breakout to $90,000 — that level now looks ambitious without a material catalyst. Watch $79,000 as immediate support; a clean close above $81,000 would shift the short-term structure.

ETH continues to underperform, down -1.31% in 24 hours and -3.95% on the week, trading at $2,303.17 on volume of $8.65B. The ETH/BTC compression story is intact and showing no sign of reversal. Among the notable divergences today, UNI was the clear standout, printing +3.28% on 24-hour volume of $0.28B — the only major ZIMR-tracked asset to post a meaningful green candle in the session. AVAX added +0.70% and BNB eked out +0.07%, while LINK was technically flat at +0.07% on $0.24B volume. The other side of the ledger is ugly: DOT dropped -1.49% and sits at $1.014, a psychologically uncomfortable handle, down -7.25% on the week. ADA at $0.203344 is off -5.78% on the week, and AVAX despite today's bounce is still -7.21% over 7 days. The message from the altcoin complex is that any green is tactical and the weekly trend remains firmly negative.

The macro context is doing most of the heavy lifting in terms of directional pressure. The Fed decision is looming, and Cointelegraph flagged FOMC and earnings season as the 2 primary risks overhanging BTC price this week. Oil retreating is a mild supportive signal for risk assets broadly, per CoinDesk, but it hasn't been enough to offset the rate uncertainty premium. The Anthropic IPO filing is an interesting adjacent data point — a blockbuster AI listing pulls institutional attention and capital allocation toward traditional equity markets at exactly the moment crypto needs macro tailwinds, and Calpers reportedly pulling back from big tech amid AI jitters adds a layer of cross-asset uncertainty that isn't crypto-specific but affects overall risk appetite. On the crypto-native side, Strategy notably skipped Bitcoin purchases this cycle and instead spent $205M on STRC buybacks according to Cointelegraph — that absence of the most visible institutional buyer is not noise.

Heading into the rest of the week, the Fed decision is the single most important binary. A hawkish hold or any revision to the rate path that pushes yields higher will hammer BTC back toward the $77,000-$78,000 range; a dovish surprise or a cut — however unlikely — would give the $90,000 bull thesis from that $68M bet some actual oxygen. The Aviva Investors launch of a tokenized share class of its $29B Sterling fund on XRP Ledger is worth monitoring as a real-world adoption signal, though XRP itself has only managed -1.01% in 24 hours and -0.42% on the week, suggesting the market is not pricing that news yet. Bernstein's call that HOOD's prediction markets will add $1.7B to revenue and exceed crypto by 2028 is a longer-horizon narrative but signals where institutional focus is drifting. The immediate risk to watch is a confirmed daily close below $79,000 on BTC — that would likely trigger a test of deeper support and drag the already-weak altcoin complex into more meaningful drawdowns.
